item.title: Boston Scientific Exposes 117,000 Records Following Voice Phishing Attack
item.description:
Boston Scientific Exposes 117,000 Records Following Voice Phishing Attack

Boston Scientific, a Massachusetts-based medical device manufacturer, is sending data breach notices to individuals after a cyberattack exposed personal and medical information belonging to 117,789 people in the United States. The incident marks the second cybersecurity event for the company this year.

🔍 Overview

The attack exposed cloud-based applications and cloud-hosted data between May 7 and May 1, 2025. Boston Scientific became aware of the unauthorized access on May 12. A subsequent investigation determined that a data breach occurred on November 5. The exposed information included personal details and medical information for individuals in multiple U.S. states.

🧩 How it works

According to notification samples shared with U.S. authorities, the hacker gained access to the company’s cloud infrastructure using social engineering in a voice phishing (vishing) attack.

⚙️ Key details

  • Data Exposed: Personal details and medical information.
  • Data Not Exposed: The notification specifies that patient medical records, data from remote monitoring systems, connected medical devices, and clinical case management or workflow applications were not exposed.
  • Scope: The incident impacted 117,789 individuals according to the Texas Attorney General breach portal.
  • Business Impact: The company stated there was no disruption to manufacturing, ordering, distribution, or service to patients and healthcare providers, and no impact on operations, performance, remote monitoring, or the safety of its products.

📊 Incident Comparison

This breach is distinct from a previous cyberattack disclosed on August 25, which caused network outages and global operational disruptions. A Boston Scientific spokesperson confirmed the most recent incident is unrelated to the August 2026 intrusion; a CrowdStrike investigation into that earlier attack found no evidence that attackers compromised cloud applications.

💡 Why it matters

As one of the world’s largest medical device manufacturers with more than 59,000 employees, 13 manufacturing facilities, and a presence in 127 countries, Boston Scientific’s data security is critical. The company contained the incident, investigated with outside cybersecurity experts, and notified law enforcement. However, the company is not offering free credit monitoring and instead recommends impacted individuals use free credit reports, place fraud alerts, and consider credit freezes.

#databreach #cybersecurity #medicaldevices #vishing #BostonScientific

Source: New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info

item.title: CIA and FinCEN Report Cyberattacks Using ARTEX Framework
item.description:
CIA and FinCEN Report Cyberattacks Using ARTEX Framework

Unknown attackers breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Additionally, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed an investigation into unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.

🔍 Overview

  • The cyberattack was reportedly carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework.
  • The incident affected the CIA, the ODNI, and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.
  • FinCEN is a US Department of the Treasury bureau that acts as the country’s official Financial Intelligence Unit and protects the nation’s financial system from illicit activities.

⚙️ Key details

  • The CIA and ODNI have not yet replied to a request for more details regarding the incident.
  • No classified data or systems were exposed in the breach.
  • A source stated, “The hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk.”
  • After detecting the attack, FinCEN took some systems offline as a precaution and told banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports, since some services may be unavailable.
  • It is unclear how the attackers gained access, when the breach occurred, or whether they stole any information from the compromised systems.

💡 Why it matters

  • These incidents follow a series of other cyberattacks that have led to security breaches at other US federal agencies in recent years.
  • One week ago, the US National Security Agency’s classified network suffered a days-long outage, which the agency attributed to scheduled routine maintenance.
  • Two years ago, the Silk Typhoon Chinese state-backed hacking group breached the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), the Treasury’s Office of Financial Research, and the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States.
  • Hackers reportedly breached the FBI’s National Crime Information Center (NCIC).
  • The ShinyHunters extortion group claimed it breached the FBI’s recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov, prompting an FBI investigation that led to the arrests of multiple suspected members.

#cybersecurity #CIA #FinCEN #AI #databreach

Source: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system

item.title: Microsoft: Azure API Management vulnerability used to steal credentials
item.description:
Microsoft: Azure API Management vulnerability used to steal credentials

Microsoft has issued a security advisory warning that a vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, with Norwegian authorities linking the flaw to cyberattacks against energy companies. The issue affects a cloud service that allows organizations to publish, secure, monitor, and manage APIs connecting applications, services, and data.

🔍 Overview

In a security advisory with Tracking ID MZK9-GH0, Microsoft stated it identified the vulnerability on November 18, 2026, and deployed a mitigation the following day. The company confirmed that customers were exposed and that an unauthorized party could have accessed secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before the issue was identified.

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected Tiers: The vulnerability specifically affects Azure API Management Classic tiers; Microsoft stated that APIM v2 tiers are not impacted.
  • Access Mechanism: The flaw allowed unauthorized access to certain management functionality when APIM Classic instances were not configured according to recommended security best practices.
  • Potential Impact: This access could allow attackers to perform administrative operations, including accessing secrets, which could potentially grant access to additional applications, services, or backend systems depending on permissions.
  • Remediation: Microsoft closed the unauthorized access path on November 19 and rotated Microsoft-controlled keys and credentials where appropriate.
  • Limitation: The remediation does not automatically invalidate customer credentials that may have been accessed before the fix was deployed.

🏛️ Reported Exploitation

Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) linked the vulnerability to attacks affecting Norwegian organizations, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi.

  • NSM Advisory: The agency stated that an unknown threat actor targeted access tokens, secrets, and named values stored in Azure API Management.
  • Discovery: NSM reported that Norway’s energy sector first discovered the vulnerability, noting that organizations in other countries and industries were also affected.
  • Equinor: The company disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on November 17, the day before Microsoft identified the vulnerability. Equinor later announced it had stopped the attack and found no indication that data had been stolen or altered.
  • Skagerak Energi: The company reported an attempted cyberattack but stated it had no impact on operations and no evidence that information was compromised.

Additionally, a Reddit post from an administrator alleged their organization detected unauthorized access to Azure Key Vault using a valid administrator token. The administrator claimed attackers exploited a zero-day authentication bypass in a deprecated legacy API to gain access to a privileged system account on APIM instances. They alleged the legacy API did not generate logs for customers to detect this access and that Microsoft initially attributed the activity to leaked customer credentials. BleepingComputer has not independently verified these allegations.

💡 Recommendations

Microsoft urged affected customers to:

  • Immediately rotate potentially exposed credentials.
  • Investigate suspicious activity in systems accessible through those credentials.
  • Review available logs for signs of unauthorized access.

NSM warned organizations to verify that their APIM instances have received the security update, noting that instances running below specific runtime versions remain vulnerable. The agency advised customers to contact their service provider if they have not received the update. Cloud security researcher Anders Kristiansen has shared threat-hunting queries to help organizations investigate potential exploitation and identify stored credentials.

#Azure #Cybersecurity #APIManagement #Vulnerability #Microsoft

Source: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers’ API credentials

item.title: Cleverbridge Breach Exposes Customer Payment Card Data
item.description:
Cleverbridge Breach Exposes Customer Payment Card Data

Cleverbridge, an e-commerce platform that provides services to software and SaaS companies, disclosed that a security breach resulted in the theft of customers’ payment card information. The stolen data includes credit card numbers and CVV security codes.

🧩 Company Background

Cleverbridge enables software and SaaS companies to sell products, process payments, and manage subscriptions. The platform lists numerous technology brands among its customers, including:

  • Red Hat
  • SUSE
  • Tenable
  • Veeam
  • Jamf
  • Sony
  • Parallels

🔍 Incident Timeline

According to a security incident disclosure, the company detected unauthorized activity on November 4, 2026. Systems were temporarily taken offline to contain the breach and were brought back online the same day. The investigation subsequently determined that a third party copied payment card data stored on the platform.

Affected customers began receiving notifications on November 20, 2026.

⚙️ Data Stolen

A breach notification shared with BleepingComputer reveals that the stolen information includes:

  • Payment card numbers
  • Expiration dates
  • CVV/CVC security codes

The notification explicitly states that no other personal data, such as names, contact details, or billing information, were copied. The notice specifies that the affected card ends in a placeholder sequence.

🚫 What Was Not Involved

Cleverbridge confirmed that the incident was not a ransomware attack. Attackers did not encrypt any of the company’s systems. The company has not disclosed how the attackers gained access, how long they remained in the systems, or the total number of affected customers.

💡 Response and Remediation

Cleverbridge has notified data protection authorities, law enforcement, payment card networks, and payment partners regarding the incident. The company is working with TransUnion’s Cyberscout to distribute breach notifications and provide affected customers with complimentary credit monitoring and fraud assistance. Customers are advised to review their payment card statements for any unauthorized transactions.

#DataBreach #Cleverbridge #PaymentSecurity #Cybersecurity #CreditCardTheft

Source: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach

item.title: Unit 42 tracks Com-affiliated vishing and data extortion campaigns
item.description:
Unit 42 tracks Com-affiliated vishing and data extortion campaigns

Unit 42 has tracked and responded to numerous waves of vishing attacks conducted by Com-affiliated threat actors in recent months, leading to data theft and extortion attempts. Since early 2026, the team has attributed multiple data theft and extortion attempts to Bling Libra and other Com-affiliated threat actors.

🔍 Overview

  • The attacks have targeted data-rich industries, such as financial services, healthcare, and legal services.
  • Targeted organizations were primarily located in the U.S., UK, and Australia.
  • Attackers use the threat group and activity cluster naming conventions tracked by Unit 42.

🧩 How it works

  • Initial Access: Attackers establish access through vishing, where they pose as internal IT support and direct employees to servers using subdomains tailored to each targeted organization.
  • MFA Bypass: These servers act as adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) proxies that pass user credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) approvals to the attackers in real time.
  • Persistence: In multiple instances, attackers have enrolled an unauthorized MFA device within minutes of authenticating to establish persistence.
  • Exfiltration: Attackers have automated data exfiltration using Python scripts to target Microsoft 365 mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint content.
  • Extortion: Following exfiltration, attackers have sent Microsoft Teams messages directly to employees, claiming data theft and directing recipients to a Tor-hosted negotiation site.

⚙️ Key details

  • CL-CRI-1264: Identified in September 2026, this activity cluster primarily targets healthcare, pharmaceutical, and other medical organizations. Attackers targeted employees on both corporate workstations and personal mobile devices, reusing a single device named “Pixel 10a” across compromised accounts.
  • CL-CRI-1274: Also identified in September 2026, this cluster avoided re-prompting for Duo MFA by replaying a persistent “keep me signed in” session token. They then used scripted access through python-requests and the Microsoft Graph SDK to collect and exfiltrate data from SharePoint and OneDrive environments. Extortion messages were sent internally via email and Microsoft Teams.
  • CL-CRI-1192: During an investigation attributed to this cluster (which Google tracks under UNC6671), a malicious browser extension named “Google Chrome” (manifest version 1.6.111) was identified. The extension was not on the Chrome Web Store and was downloaded from an attacker-controlled server at oskeysetup[.]com, requiring manual sideloading using Developer Mode.

💡 Why it matters

  • Organizations can access tailored adversary intelligence, direct analyst consultations, and specialized exposure tracking through Unit 42 Threat Intel Services and its Deep and Dark Web Service.
  • If an organization thinks it might have been compromised or has an urgent matter, it should contact the Unit 42 Incident Response team.

#Unit42 #ThreatIntel #Vishing #Com-affiliated #Cybersecurity

Source: Dialing for Data: Inside the Com’s High-Profile Heists

item.title: How AWS Security Incident Response triages threat findings from GuardDuty
item.description:
How AWS Security Incident Response triages threat findings from GuardDuty

AWS Security Incident Response continuously triages threat findings from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub CSPM, a process where most work never surfaces as a customer-facing case. The service ingests these findings through Amazon EventBridge rules automatically deployed during onboarding, ensuring that active threats are evaluated while posture and compliance issues remain in existing remediation processes.

🧩 How it works

The automated triage process evaluates each finding payload against several data sources to determine if an activity is benign or requires action.

  • Data sources: The service assesses the finding payload, related AWS activity from AWS CloudTrail and Amazon VPC Flow Logs, AWS threat intelligence, and user-provided environment context.
  • Benchmarking: Findings are mapped against a profile of known-good activity specific to the customer’s environment.
  • Third-party integration: Findings from tools like CrowdStrike, Trend Micro, or Lacework sent to Security Hub CSPM are also ingested, provided they carry complete payload information including resource ID, account ID, timestamp, and threat details. GuardDuty findings are ingested directly to prevent duplication.

⚙️ Key details

Outcomes of the triage process vary depending on the nature of the finding. Posture and compliance findings, such as misconfigurations or failed benchmark checks, are not triaged as they reflect environment state rather than active threats. They remain current without archiving and do not generate cases.

For active threat findings, such as compromised credentials, cryptomining, or data exfiltration, the service determines one of three dispositions:

Disposition Trigger Condition Action Taken
Archived, no action needed Automated triage or engineer confirms activity is benign or expected Finding is archived in GuardDuty; no case is created and no customer contact is made
Proactive case opened Triage cannot confirm activity is benign Case is opened as “Unconfirmed Activity” or “Inappropriate/Unintended Activity”; incident response team is engaged; finding stays Current until resolved
Retained for review Posture-related findings (e.g., overly permissive policies) No case is created; finding remains Current without archiving

When a proactive case is opened, customers respond via the AWS Management Console under the Cases section, allowing direct communication, context sharing, and case resolution. For third-party findings ingested through Security Hub CSPM, the disposition logic mirrors GuardDuty, but the status changes from NEW to NOTIFIED when triage begins, moving to SUPPRESSED if cleared as benign.

💡 Why it matters

The service builds a profile of what is normal in your environment to distinguish between expected behavior and genuine threats. For example, if GuardDuty flags an “UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS” finding, the service checks if the external IP belongs to a known corporate VPN range. If the pattern is recognized, the finding is archived. If the IP is from a hosting provider with no prior association and the IAM role has never called from outside AWS, a proactive case is created for investigation. Across customers, less than 1 percent of ingested findings result in a customer-facing escalation.

#AWS #Security #GuardDuty #IncidentResponse #ThreatDetection

Source: How AWS Security Incident Response triages your security findings | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Ransomware Defense: Detecting Pre-Encryption Attack Stages
item.description:
Ransomware Defense: Detecting Pre-Encryption Attack Stages

Ransomware attacks rarely begin with the ransomware payload itself. Operators first need an initial foothold, and common entry paths include exploitation of vulnerable internet-facing systems, abuse of stolen credentials, and social engineering. By the time encryption occurs, the intrusion may already include credential theft, privilege escalation, defense evasion, recovery sabotage, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. In data-extortion attacks, encryption may never happen at all, as operators steal data and threaten to leak it without encrypting anything.

🚀 Initial Entry Paths

Attacker entry into environments typically occurs through three primary vectors:

  • Vulnerable Systems: Unpatched, externally accessible services provide a route into the environment.
  • Stolen Credentials: Compromised credentials allow attackers to enter through legitimate remote-access or cloud services.
  • Social Engineering: This path targets users and the processes surrounding identity and access.

Once attackers establish access, they use stolen credentials and legitimate administration tools to move through victim environments before deploying ransomware.

🔍 Pre-Encryption Detection Signals

Defenders need to detect behaviors that precede encryption, not only the encryptor itself. Five high-value signals deserve immediate attention when monitoring for suspicious post-compromise behavior:

Signal Description
Defense tampering Attempts to stop security services, modify protection agents, load vulnerable drivers, or clear event logs.
Privilege escalation and lateral movement Unexpected privileged accounts, remote-execution tools spreading across hosts, or unusual server-to-server remote access.
Data exfiltration Unusual outbound transfers from systems that do not normally upload large volumes of data.
Recovery sabotage Deletion of shadow copies, backup catalogs, or recovery options using tools such as vssadmin.exe, wbadmin.exe, or bcdedit.exe.
Pre-encryption file behavior Rapid file enumeration, repeated read-write-rename activity, and encryption-like changes across local or network locations.

⚙️ Layered Defense Strategy

Stopping ransomware is rarely about a single control. A comprehensive strategy requires reducing opportunities for initial compromise, detecting and containing malicious activity when they do occur, and having a reliable way to recover if systems or data are affected.

  • Prevention: Reducing unnecessary internet exposure, prioritizing patching of high-risk systems, strengthening identity and access controls, and protecting email and collaboration channels.
  • Detection and Response: Monitoring endpoints for suspicious post-compromise behavior provides a layer when preventive controls do not stop the initial intrusion. Endpoint protection, email security, and extended detection and response (XDR) tools can identify and contain malicious activity across endpoints, email, and the wider environment.
  • Recovery: Integrated backup and recovery provide the path to restoring affected systems and data. It is important to note that this layer does not undo data theft, a critical distinction in double-extortion attacks.

#Ransomware #Cybersecurity #ThreatDetection #DataExfiltration

Source: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
